Trump Dumped Micron, Up 338% in a Year. The Memory Cycle Decides Who's Right ©Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok and Adam Smigielski from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

President Trump's brokerage accounts sold $251,000 to $515,000 of Micron stock in August, plus $1 million to $5 million of AMD, and bought as much as $25.3 million of Meta Platforms.

Outside managers run those accounts, but selling Micron is still a bet that the memory shortage behind its run is near its peak.

Micron's gross margin went from 2.7% in fiscal 2023 to 80.7% in fiscal 2026, which shows how much its profits depend on memory prices.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to more than double to $176.55 in fiscal 2027, so the numbers say the sale came early, and Micron's next report is the test.

Micron Technology (MU:NASDAQ) is up 338% in a year, and a new disclosure shows President Trump's portfolio heading for the exit.

His accounts sold Micron in August, sold Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) that month too, and made their biggest purchase in Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ).

What exactly happened

Trump's newest filing with the Office of Government Ethics lists 517 trades. Three of them stand out:

Micron: net sales of $251,000 to $515,000

AMD: a sale of $1 million to $5 million

Meta: net purchases of $5.1 million to $25.3 million, the month's largest buy

Third-party firms manage these accounts, so Trump didn't make the call himself. And next to the Meta purchase, the Micron sale is small potatoes.

But it's the most interesting one to me for the very simple reason that…whoever sold made a real bet on the memory cycle. After a 338% year, every Micron holder is making that same bet, one way or the other.

Margins show where the cycle stands

Memory is a commodity. As Morningstar analyst William Kerwin wrote, "We view DRAM and NAND as commodity-like products prone to market supply/demand dynamics and steady pricing erosion."

You can see it in Micron's gross margin. It fell to 2.7% in fiscal 2023, then climbed to 80.7% in fiscal 2026 as AI demand ran into a memory shortage…

Micron Technology (MU): gross margin (%), fiscal 2022–2026 (years to August) (TIKR)

That's far above the 45.2% from fiscal 2022. (And I mean, fiscal 2023 hardly bears mentioning, right?)

The latest quarter shows the shortage at full tilt. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenue rose 379% to $54 billion. Adjusted EPS came in at $33.42, up from $3.03 a year earlier.

When the shortage eases, memory prices fall, and Micron's earnings fall with them. Selling now is a bet that day is close.

Analysts don't see a peak yet

Wall Street expects profits to keep climbing for two more years. Consensus has normalized EPS going from $75.52 in fiscal 2026 to $176.55 in fiscal 2027 (35 analysts), and then to $206.89 in fiscal 2028 (36 analysts)…

title: Meta Stock Climbed 25% in September. Here’s Why There’s More Upside Ahead
detail:
Meta Stock Climbed 25% in September. Here’s Why There’s More Upside Ahead
Prosper Junior Bakiny, The Motley Fool
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:55 AM MST 5 min read
META
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

After lagging the market over the past year, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is finally bouncing back. During September -- a month that has historically not been great for equity markets -- Meta gained about 25%, while the S&P 500 climbed by less than 1%. Meta has given back some of these gains in October, but for investors focused on the long game, there could be plenty of upside left for the tech leader. Here is why.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Meta's heavy investments are paying off

Over the past year, Meta Platforms has gone all in on artificial intelligence (AI). The company's significant investments in this field have been somewhat reminiscent of the period when it poured substantial sums into its metaverse ambitions. There is only one problem. Meta Platforms' metaverse efforts did not quite yield the results management expected.

So, it's not surprising that the market was somewhat skeptical of Meta's new focus, which is harming the bottom line. In the second quarter, Meta Platforms' revenue grew by 28% year over year to $60.8 billion. So far so good. However, the company's income from operations dropped 8% year over year to $18.8 billion, with the operating margin at 31%, down from 43% in the year-ago period.

Meta Platforms' net income dropped 14% year over year to $15.8 billion, and the company's free cash flow declined 91% to $784 million. Meta's AI investments were partly responsible for the declining profits. The question for investors is whether the company's spending will pay off and justify its investments.

Recent developments suggest that Meta's spending wasn't in vain. Last month, the company launched Muse, an AI agent that quickly became popular and rose to the top of the list of the most downloaded free iOS apps. Muse can help its users perform a host of tasks and is proactive -- it can act autonomously without a prompt, unlike AI chatbots. The service is free up to certain usage limits. There is a paid tier for those who want more capabilities.

Meta also suggested that it would monetize Muse by charging retailers a transaction fee when the AI agent helps users make purchases. But Meta didn't stop there. The company launched Muse for small businesses. More recently, the company launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, two advanced AI models that are on par with the leaders in the field, according to some rankings.

META Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

To justify the Street's most aggressive views, Meta needs three things in this quarter: revenue at or above the top of its $61B to $64B guide, ad pricing that holds near Q2's +12% gain, and no higher drift in the $130B to $145B capex range.

Q2 Revenue Beat Masked by an EPS Miss and Vanishing Free Cash Flow

Shares fell 3.72% in the latest session and 1.3% on the week, yet remain up 5.42% over a month and 7.72% year to date. The stock trades 9% below its 52-week high of $779.82 while sitting 36.6% above its low of $519.37.

In Q2, revenue rose 27.96% to $60.80B, beating estimates, but EPS of $6.18 missed the $7.2173 consensus, ending a six-quarter beat run. A $2.40B legal charge and $1.18B in severance weighed, while free cash flow shrank to $784 million.
